newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-BARCELONA BEAT EXTREMADURA TO MAINTAIN TITLE HOPES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BARCELONA BEAT EXTREMADURA TO MAINTAIN TITLE HOPES.

text.p: Barcelona maintained their faint hopes of taking the Spanish league championship on Monday with a hard-fought 3-1 victory at Extremadura.
The win leaves Barcelona eight points adrift of leaders Real Madrid ahead of Saturday's eagerly-awaited clash between the two arch-rivals.
Barcelona struck in the 10th minute when Ronaldo appeared unmarked on the right, and Extremadura keeper Navarro Montoya was unable to hang on to his shot.
The home side scored a well-deserved equaliser just after the half-hour after Silvani slipped through to beat Vitor Baia.
But Barcelona struck straight back through Luis Enrique Martinez, who met a long cross from Hristo Stoichkov to loop a fine header over Montoya.
Luis Enrique sealed the game 10 minutes from time, capitalising on a fine pass from Ronaldo after the Extremadura defence had failed to clear a corner.
